I mentioned this in another thread but it's worth reiterating here.

I have not been on the IRC because my IP address would be visible to all users assuming I didn't take precautions such as using a BNC (basically an IRC proxy), Tor, or something of that ilk.

I strongly recommend you guys consider this if you are in any way interested in using the IRC service.

I always keep a VPN handy, would that work?

If so, is there any other way that connecting to that shithole could affect either my computer or my privacy beyond that?

Basically, the IP address you connect with is easily accessible by anybody who wants it. If you're happy for everyone to know the outgoing IP address of your VPN connection, then you're fine. I'm assuming you're familiar with the potential repercussions of anyone knowing your IP address already. How much you care is up to you.

Most IRC clients show your IP (or sometimes reverse DNS) next to your chosen nickname when you join or leave a channel. Anybody at any time can use the command /whois (yournick) to gain that information also, you don't have to be in the same channel, just on the same IRC network.

If I was going to connect to it, at bare minimum I would use Tor, and make damn sure I knew I had it configured correctly. All it takes is to connect once without it, and they have your IP address and quite possibly your approximate location.

There are also providers of BNCs ("IRC bouncers") which would be suitable to protect yourself against this kind of thing, but generally these are only used by proper IRC junkies.

Because IRC has been around for a very long time, and is stereotypically used by techies, geeks and hackers, the clients available are generally well written, secure, and battle hardened. I haven't used IRC on Windows in probably a decade or more, but the most prominent Windows client at that time was called mIRC, I assume it's still around. It is possible to find out what IRC client (and therefore, in almost all cases, the OS too) any user is running, although if I remember rightly, you will be notified that someone has queried that information.

I haven't been on IRC in a while though, and I have never connected to an IRC network I believed to be overly suspect or otherwise adversarial. I can't comment on specifics regarding how they have set this IRC network up. It is possible they have it set up to hide client IP addresses but I have seen screenshots which imply otherwise.

I don't care about my VPN IP being seen, as I'm pretty sure I'm not winning the lottery in finding someone that can actually do something with that information.
